This is a petition seeking quashing of the FIR No. 624/2019 dated 31.12.2019 registered at PS Dayalpur under Section 498A/406/34 IPC and proceedings emanating therefrom.

2. During the pendency of the proceedings, the parties have arrived at a settlement dated 15.03.2022 before the Delhi Mediation Centre, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi, pursuant to which, the petitioner was to pay a total sum of Rs. 2,50,000/- to the respondent No.2.

sentences.text:
It is agreed between the parties that husband shall pay a total sum of Rs,
2,50,000/- (Rupees Two Lakh Fifty Thousand only) to the wife towards her all claims including, dowry articles, Mehar, Iddat, permanent alimony and maintenance (present, past and future) etc. for herself as well as for upbringing and welfare of minor son Mohd. Hassan.

3. It is agreed between the parties that husband shall make the payment of settled amount of Rs. 2,50,000/- to the wife in two installments i.e. Rs. 1,50,000/- (Rupees One Lakh Fifty Thousand only) by way of cash/DD, on or before 29.03.2022 at the time of withdrawal of the present maintenance petition as well as the Execution petition, mentioned above.

The amount of Rs.
1,00,000/- shall be given in the name of the minor child Mohd. Hassan in the shape of an FDR which can only be encashed after he attains the age of majority.
However, the interest accrued thereon shall be used by the petitioner for the education and upbringing of the child."

4. The same is contrary to the judgment of 'Ganesh vs. Sudhirkumar Srivastava' [(2020) 20 SCC 787].
5. The petitioner and the respondent No.2 state that the settlement and this order shall not come in the way of minor child, namely, Mohd. Hassan This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 24/09/2023 at 20:42:21 to claim his rights of inheritance, maintenance, education, marriage etc. against either of the parties.
6. The petitioner is present in Court and has been identified by Mr. Sunil Kumar, learned counsel.
7. The respondent No.2 is also present in Court and has been identified by Mr. Kapil Sarkar, learned counsel.
8. The parties state that they have arrived at a settlement out of their own free will and without any undue influence, threat, pressure or coercion.
9. The respondent No.2 has no objection if the present FIR is quashed.

10. Taking their statements on record and binding the parties to the same, the FIR No. 624/2019 dated 31.12.2019 registered at PS Dayalpur under Section 498A/406/34 IPC and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom are hereby quashed.
11. The petition is disposed of in the aforesaid terms.
JASMEET SINGH, J MAY 22, 2023 /
